title: Овощи аль денте и куртка Кости  (Al Dente Vegetables and Kostya's Jacket)

segments.t: Behind the restaurant by the dumpsters, homeless gourmet Rodion Sergeyevich tastes the kitchen's discarded food and remarks that the vegetables are overcooked instead of true al dente. When Chef Barinov scolds Max using Rodion's exact words, Nastya asks Kostya to lend her his warm jacket to step outside.
Дошли за счет своей внутренней температуры.
Костик, отдай мне свою куртку, пожалуйста.
А что мне за это будет?
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
Дошли за счет своей внутренней температуры.

'They finished cooking from their own internal heat.' Emphasizing the temperature before Nastya, Kostya centers the thought on "temperatury" ("temperature", from "temperatura") without wasting a word.
'And some kind of stew.' Nastya responds evenly facing Kostya, watching Kostya's face to see how the news lands.
'That is the cook's doing.' Bringing up the cook before Nastya, Kostya centers the thought on "povara" ("cook", from "povar") without wasting a word.
'Nastya gave it to me.' Replying openly around Nastya, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Why are the two of you hanging around out here?' Kostya probes earnestly what Nastya is actually getting at here.
'Go learn how to cook properly.' Nastya speaks directly with Kostya and uses "gotovit" ("to cook") to carry the main weight of the thought.
'A very competent person told me.' Opening up quietly beside Nastya, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 4 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'That your vegetables are supposed to be al dente.' Nastya speaks up frankly without holding back, making her position completely clear.
'Just like...' Stepping in dryly in the exchange, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'I am heading back in.' Weighing in naturally right here, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
Костик, отдай мне свою куртку, пожалуйста.
'Kostik, lend me your jacket, please.' Nastya cuts in lightly on the spot, watching Kostya's face to see how the news lands.
'I need to step outside for a minute.' Addressing the street before Kostya, Nastya reaches for the Russian word "ulitsu" ("street", built from "ulitsa") right at the center of the line.
А что мне за это будет?
'And what do I get in return for that?' Answering evenly before Nastya, Kostya puts the question word "chto" right at the start so Nastya hears the focus immediately.
Дошли за счет своей внутренней температуры.
Костик, отдай мне свою куртку, пожалуйста.
А что мне за это будет?
That wraps up this scene as in the courtyard, homeless gourmet Rodion Sergeyevich critiques Max's overcooked vegetables, and Nastya asks to borrow Kostya's warm jacket. See you next time!
